title: SWR family
idea: SWR tells you how well the antenna system matches the feed line. 1:1 is perfect. The higher it goes, the worse the match, and a solid-state radio turns its power down to protect itself.

items: A measure of how well a load is matched to a transmission line
A solid-state radio reduces power to protect its output transistors, so you see low power
A loose connection in the antenna or feed line
Matches the antenna system impedance to the transceiver's output impedance

config.heading: What is the SWR telling you?
config.lead: Pick what you see on the meter or the radio.

situations.label: The meter reads 1:1
situations.title: A perfect match
situations.text: 1:1 means the antenna and the feed line are perfectly matched in impedance. Not zero, and not 50:50.

situations.label: The meter reads 4:1
situations.title: An impedance mismatch
situations.text: A high reading like 4:1 means the impedances don't match. It isn't a gain or loss in dB.

situations.label: My solid-state radio's power dropped
situations.title: Probably high SWR
situations.text: Past a certain SWR, most solid-state transmitters reduce output power to protect the RF output amplifier transistors. Low SWR doesn't cause low power.

situations.label: The SWR keeps jumping around
situations.title: A loose connection
situations.text: Erratic changes in SWR point to a loose connection in the antenna or the feed line.

situations.label: The radio and antenna don't match
situations.title: An antenna tuner
situations.text: An antenna tuner, or coupler, matches the antenna system's impedance to the transceiver's output impedance.

situations.label: I want to measure SWR
situations.title: A directional wattmeter
situations.text: A directional wattmeter can be used to determine SWR. A voltmeter or ohmmeter can't.

compare.how: Mismatch. A solid-state radio cuts its power.
Something is loose in the antenna or feed line.

traps.why: Low SWR is good. It's high SWR that makes a solid-state radio cut power.
SWR is a ratio. A perfect match reads 1:1, not zero.

traps.wrong: To lower the SWR on the transmission line
traps.why: Cutting power doesn't change the SWR. It protects the output transistors.
SWR isn't measured in dB. 4:1 just means a mismatch.
A voltmeter can't tell forward from reflected power. Use a directional wattmeter.

traps.wrong: It automatically selects the proper antenna for the frequency band being used
traps.why: A tuner doesn't pick the antenna. It matches the antenna system to the radio's impedance.
Weather doesn't make SWR jump around. A loose connection does.

traps.wrong: An indication of the quality of your station’s ground connection
traps.why: SWR is about the match between the load and the line, not your ground.
